title: Subtree of Another Tree
oneLinerQuestion: Determine if a binary tree is structurally and value-wise identical to a subtree of another.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Subtree of Another Tree problem asks whether a binary tree `subRoot` is structurally identical with identical node values to a subtree of `root`. A subtree must consist of a node in `root` and all of its descendants down to the leaves. We break this problem into two recursive layers: an outer tree traversal that visits each node in `root` as a candidate subtree root, and an inner helper function (`isSameTree`) that evaluates structural and value equality between two trees. If the candidate subtree starting at the current node matches `subRoot` entirely, we return true; otherwise, we search recursively in the left and right subtrees of `root`.

- Step 1: Base Case Guards for Outer Function — In `isSubtree(root, subRoot)`: if `subRoot === null`, an empty tree is vacuously a subtree of any tree, returning `true`. If `root === null` while `subRoot !== null`, `root` cannot contain `subRoot`, returning `false`.

- Step 2: Helper Function Definition (isSameTree) — Define `isSameTree(p, q)`: if both `p === null` and `q === null`, return `true` (both subtrees terminated simultaneously). If one is `null` while the other is not, or `p.val !== q.val`, return `false` (structural mismatch or value inequality). Otherwise, return `isSameTree(p.left, q.left) && isSameTree(p.right, q.right)`.

- Step 3: Current Node Equality Check — For the current `root`, test if the subtree starting here matches `subRoot`: `if (isSameTree(root, subRoot)) return true`.

- Step 4: Recursive Branch Exploration — If the current node is not an identical match, recursively check whether `subRoot` is contained in either child subtree: `return isSubtree(root.left, subRoot) || isSubtree(root.right, subRoot)`.

- Step 5: Termination & Result Delivery — The recursion halts early as soon as any matching subtree returns `true`. If all nodes in `root` are exhausted without a match, the function concludes with `false`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(R * S) where R is the number of nodes in `root` and S is the number of nodes in `subRoot`, as for each of the R nodes we may traverse up to S nodes during equality checking (can be optimized to O(R + S) via Merkle tree hashing or KMP on serialized preorder traversals). Space Complexity: O(H_root) auxiliary space on the call stack, where H_root is the height of `root` (bounded by O(R) in a skewed tree).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isSubtree(root, subRoot):
    IF subRoot IS NULL THEN RETURN True
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN False
    IF isSameTree(root, subRoot) THEN RETURN True
    RETURN isSubtree(root.left, subRoot) OR isSubtree(root.right, subRoot)
END FUNCTION
